_comment: How to read a page whose shape the generic reader cannot handle. Each rule applies to every page whose URL matches urlPattern. See docs/specs/coverage-extraction.md for the fields. A recipe that stops producing what it promises is reported, never silently dropped.

rules.note: Three lists, not one. External access enumerates 15 resource types under its own heading, internal access 6 under another, and the unused access analyzer states its two in a single sentence in the opening Note with no heading at all: 'Unused access analyzers only support IAM users and roles.'

One H2 per Region listing the controls unavailable there. Read per control that is 6,313 statements about 589 individual controls, which would need a row each. At the feature level it says: Security Hub controls apply in this Region, with some unavailable — so one claim per Region, carrying the count.
The full catalogue of AWS Config managed rules, one bullet each.
Each H2 is one active GuardDuty finding type. The retired page is read by its own rule, because it states the opposite.

The table publishes two catalogues side by side: 166 managed data identifiers and the sensitive data types they detect. A type is not an identifier, so they are counted separately rather than merged onto one axis.
Rule group names appear only in inline code, as Name: `AWSManagedRules…`. The changelog and index pages are excluded: neither states capability.

Thirteen scanners on one page, each with its own list. EC2 splits agentless from agent-based, ECR splits basic from enhanced, and CIS scanning, the Scan API, the VM Scanner and the SSM plugin each support a different set again. One merged row stated the widest list for all of them.

recipes.onlyBlocksMatching: programming languages: Amazon Inspector SSM plugin

rules.note: The S3 storage classes Macie reads, and the file formats it can open. Extensions are comma separated inside one cell.

select.pattern: (S3 Glacier Deep Archive|S3 Express One Zone)

rules.note: Which S3 features Malware Protection for S3 can and cannot handle. Several features share one cell, joined by a line break.

The Applications column is the universe: the Ecosystems column is a vendor grouping where one row holds fifteen Microsoft products and another holds one. The page is about applications installed outside a package manager, so these are not package ecosystems.
Each standard is a bold-led bullet: the name sits before the dash.
The prebuilt audit frameworks Audit Manager ships.
The AWS log sources Security Lake can ingest natively.
The Category column of the threat signature rule group table.
Which AWS services support trusted access with Organizations. Yes and No arrive as icons, which the parser turns back into words.
The AWS services that use Secrets Manager secrets.
These finding types are retired: the page says GuardDuty no longer generates them. Recording them as covered asserted the inverse.
GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring finding types, one per H2.
EKS Protection finding types.
Malware Protection for EC2 finding types.
Malware Protection for AWS Backup finding types.
RDS Protection finding types.
Lambda Protection finding types.
AI Protection finding types.
Attack sequence finding types, emitted by Extended Threat Detection.
Both fraud-control rule groups state the same exclusion: they cannot protect Amazon Cognito user pools.

select.sentenceMatches: is ?n'?t available for use with Amazon Cognito

rules.note: Two lists in one page. The bullets say what Shield Advanced protects; two notes say what it does not. A Gateway Load Balancer and a custom routing accelerator have the same CloudFormation type as the load balancers and accelerators Shield does protect, so those types come out partial, which is the accurate reading: covered for some of that type, not for others.

select.sentenceMatches: can't (use Shield Advanced to protect|protect)|handle outbound traffic only
select.pattern: (AWS Global Accelerator custom routing accelerators|Gateway Load Balancers|NAT Gateways)

rules.note: Six capabilities in one table. Each column is a separate statement about the same resource types, so each is its own row: merging them into one asserted that whatever the first column said held for all of them. AWS managed permissions has no column — the legend states it holds for every supported resource type.
Five capabilities in one table, one per column. Each is its own row: a single row could only state one of the five, and stated it for all.
Two headings, two platform lists. The earlier split was by CPU architecture, which is a column inside each table rather than the division the page makes.
Resource type by Region. The types run down the first column and the Regions across the header, so every cell is one statement.
One H2 per Region listing the managed rules available there. Collapsed to one claim per Region carrying the rule count, rather than a statement per rule.
The authoritative reference of every resource type AWS Config records, in the Resource Type Value column.
Every Security Hub CSPM control. Without this the map held only the per-Region exclusions, so the feature read as zero controls covered.

One heading holds two lists. The control plane operations that create and manage a Multi-Region Access Point all carry MultiRegionAccessPoint in their name; the data plane operations that accept its ARN do not. They are separate statements and get separate rows.

The OIDC access scope catalogue, and only that. The table's third column names the service each scope belongs to; that is a per-scope qualifier, not a claim that IAM Identity Center applications reach five of the 526 AWS services. Reading it as service coverage was a fabrication and the column is left alone.

An AWS Shield network security director page that sits in the AWS WAF guide, so its Region table was landing on wafv2/service-linked-roles. The recipe hands the page to Shield and reads the whole table. The bullets above it describe what the role may call, not what the service covers.

recipes.qualifier: AWS Shield network security director is in preview; Region support may change.

rules.note: The foundational data sources GuardDuty reads, one per H2. This is coverage on an axis outside GuardDuty: these logs exist whether or not GuardDuty does.

Every statement on this page sits under a bold subject naming what it is about: a protection plan, an API, or one finding type. Reading the sentences without that subject put all of them on a catch-all 'GuardDuty findings' row, which then read '2 excluded of 46' — a claim about GuardDuty findings as a whole that the page never makes. Only the protection-plan exclusions are feature-level coverage. A finding type missing from one Region is a fact about that one catalogue member, and we count catalogues rather than measuring them, so those are not published.
Each H2 is one KMS condition key. kms:ViaService additionally lists the AWS services it accepts, and those services are that one key's coverage — not the coverage of condition keys in general.

A matrix: one row per AWS service, one column per IAM capability, each cell Yes, No or Partial. Each column is a distinct capability, so each gets its own feature; collapsing them into one row answered six questions with one number.
The Regions where the ACM service-linked role can be used. This is the SLR's limit, not where ACM runs, so it belongs to the SLR feature.
This is the AWS WAF Classic service-linked role page, so it belongs to the WAF Classic service, not to WAFv2.
Where the AWSServiceRoleForArtifact role can be used. The page says outright this is not where AWS Artifact is available, and its third column says Yes for only three Regions.
The finding types that can trigger a GuardDuty-initiated malware scan, one per H2.
The Regions where AWS Private CA offers a PrivateLink endpoint.
The Regions where CloudTrail Lake is available.

The page lists the event sources that emit network activity events, one backticked service principal per bullet. The principal is the unambiguous identifier; the prose service names beside it are not all present.
The Regions where CloudTrail is available.
The Regions where AWS Config is available.
The Regions where the Directory Service service-linked role can be used.

Two tables, seven columns, seven separate availabilities. The directory types reach 38 Regions; the Directory Service Data API reaches 18. Reading the Region column alone and calling it the service as a whole published 38 for all seven, which is wrong for the three Directory Service Data rows.
The Regions where the Security Incident Response service-linked roles can be used.
The Regions where Verified Access offers FIPS endpoints.

The ATP page names exactly two resource types: CloudFront distributions, the only place the rule group also inspects responses, and Amazon Cognito user pools, which it explicitly cannot protect. The exclusion is read by the shared fraud-control recipe; this one reads the supported side.

select.pattern: For (CloudFront distributions), in addition to inspecting incoming login requests

rules.note: Each managed rule group publishes its own rules in a 'Rule name' table. That is a catalogue the rule group owns, so it is counted, not measured — the page states no per-rule availability.
